method: I used the real renderer: render_bench in real Chrome, Metal GPU, heavy slot, 1/60 s frames. Each test fighter ran on its own match host with waves, Wicks and other seats moved off the RIFT Mid Road (y 55). It was ordered 40 m east from x 62. To set the speed I set its slowPow / hastePow so that speed = r x the renderer's own runRef (actor.runRef), then measured r back from the body's travel (it matched to 0.001). Per foot, the ankle (foot bone) and the toe (toe bone) height was taken above the actor root. A contact span is the point within 3 cm of its 5th-percentile height for 4 or more frames, and spans touching the capture's ends are dropped. Slip is the point's net horizontal travel over the span divided by the body's travel. I also recorded the summed path length, which is stricter. 'Live' means the ./deploy catalog (2026.11.19 GLBs) on a second frozen server, with the actor's run floor set back to live's 0.35. git diff 2baec0ec0..HEAD -- src shows that this floor is the only code difference, so this is exactly live's code path. Leg spikes: for each frame I took the angular step of the thigh and shin local rotations, then the frame's excess over its larger neighbour. The ramp runs 0.15 -> 1.6 -> 0.15 x runRef over 12 s and then stops.
problems: The bar is met everywhere. Median slip (ankle / toe, % of body speed) on HEAD at r = 0.30 / 0.40 / 0.50 / 0.60 / 0.72 / 0.85 / 1.0 / 1.3 / 1.5. Ervet: 5.4/3.6, 5.1/3.6, 5.5/3.6, 4.7/3.8, 4.6/3.8, 4.8/3.9, 4.7/3.7, 4.6/4.1, 4.7/4.0. Rishal: 5.3/3.0, 5.0/3.1, 5.0/3.1, 4.7/3.0, 4.7/3.1, 4.7/3.1, 4.6/3.3, 4.8/3.5, 5.3/3.3. The worst single contact span at any speed is 6.5 % (Ervet ankle at 0.85), and the cap is 18 %. Each speed had 13-38 spans per point, and the path stayed straight (lateral deviation <= 1.7 cm).

Live, the same way: Ervet's toe 16.1-18.5 % at 0.4-1.5 (ankle 2.5-4.9) and 10.7 % ankle at 0.30 (under the 0.35 floor). Rishal's toe 20.7-24.0 % and ankle 15-32 % (spans up to 37.7 %); at r 1.0 he had no contact span at all. HEAD cuts every live slide by 3-6x. These are independent numbers and they agree with the implementer's table to within 0.3 points.

Unslowed run (no status): Ervet HEAD 4.5/4.1 vs live 4.2/16.1. Rishal HEAD 4.7/3.2 vs live 31.5/22.6. This is better than live. Visible side effect: the renderer's runRef changed (Ervet 3.53 -> 3.30, Rishal 4.45 -> 3.68). At normal speed Ervet's legs now cycle 7 % faster than live and Rishal's 21 % faster (timeScale 0.977 -> 1.045 and 0.798 -> 0.965). That faster cycle is what makes the feet match the ground. It reads as a planted run, not as hurrying.

Blend thresholds and no freeze. These two have no walk, so the only thresholds are the run floor (now 0.13) and the haste layer at 1.3 x runRef. On the ramp, timeScale moves at most 0.008 per frame and no frame has moving body with still legs (0 frozen frames for both, either direction, and through the stop). Worst one-frame excess on the ramp, thigh / shin: Ervet HEAD 3.5 / 8.2 deg vs live 4.2 / 6.8. Rishal HEAD 4.2 / 9.4 deg vs live 14.7 / 25.3 (live Rishal had a real knee pop on the ramp; it is gone).

Minor, not a blocker: Ervet's hasted run at 1.3-1.5 x has a one-frame shin step of 19-22 deg against 12-14 either side (excess 7-8 deg). Live has 14-16 against 8-9 (excess 6-7.5). This is about the same as live and is the fast knee fold of a sprint. Ervet's thigh is clean, so it is not the touchdown snap round 1 found. Rishal at 1.3-1.5 x: 7.0-7.8 deg excess, against 20-25 on live. At the 24.5 m and 31 m cameras I could not see it in the frame strips.

Minor: on the path-length measure, which counts every centimetre of in-span jitter and roll, Rishal's toe reads 12.7-15.4 % and his ankle 8.9-12.8 %. Ervet reads 6.1-7.2 % toe and 8.0-11.1 % ankle. Live reads 17.7-25 % toe on Ervet and 21-34 % on Rishal. The net-travel bar (the method in verify_anim_r2/r3) is met with a wide margin. The path figure is the heel-and-toe roll inside the contact that the ruling's 'not done' already mentions, and it is far better than live.

I looked at the frame strips: 10 frames over 1.2 cycles. Both fighters at r 0.3 / 0.6 / 1.0 / 1.5 at the 31 m match camera, plus a close look at 4K (the camera clamps at 24.5 m, giving body crops about 356 px tall), on HEAD and live. Every skin of both fighters was shot at the 31 m camera. The legs cycle believably at every speed: a crouched planted run on Rishal, with the knees driving and the feet landing and pushing off. There is no glide, no moonwalk, no tiny shuffle at speed, no knee snap, and nothing goes through the floor. Ervet's cloak covers most of her legs at the match camera, so her run reads as on live with the boots holding the ground. Rishal's slowed run on HEAD reads as planted; on live his feet visibly skate.
